articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI support bot got socially engineered harder than a fresh intern at DEF CON, letting hackers seize Instagram accounts including Obama's White House page. When your chatbot has worse OpSec than a drunk CEO on Twitter, maybe it's time to rethink automation.

articles.title: Welcome New EFF Executive Director Nicole Ozer
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually dropped AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like classified docs at a coffee shop. The agency tasked with protecting America's infrastructure couldn't protect their own credentials from public embarrassment.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: License plate readers have officially jumped the shark—now they're stalking kids for school enrollment and noise complaints. Mission creep meets surveillance state in the dystopian crossover nobody asked for.

articles.title: Patch Now: Another Palo Alto Auth Bypass Bug Under Active Exploit
articles.summary: Microsoft threatens criminal charges against researcher who published zero-days, because apparently shooting the messenger is easier than fixing broken code. Nothing says 'responsible disclosure' like legal intimidation.

articles.title: Name That Toon: Mark of (Cybersecurity) Progress
articles.summary: Palo Alto's GlobalProtect VPN got pwned again with another auth bypass bug under active exploitation. At this point, their security track record makes Internet Explorer look bulletproof.

articles.title: New York Comptroller’s Trip to Israel Raised Ethical Concerns, State Commission Said
articles.summary: Philly cops admit they're tracking 'First Amendment activity' critical of AI data centers. When exercising constitutional rights becomes a surveillance target, the cyberpunk dystopia officially arrived ahead of schedule.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: New Linux Flaw, PAN-OS Exploit, AI-Powered Attacks, OAuth Phishing and More
articles.summary: Red Hat npm packages got wormed by Miasma supply chain attack, stealing dev credentials faster than you can say 'trusted repository.' When even the enterprise Linux vendor's ecosystem gets compromised, trust nothing.

articles.title: Microsoft threatens legal action against researcher Nightmare Eclipse for exploit disclosure
articles.summary: CVE-2026-0257 lets attackers forge Palo Alto VPN cookies like a digital bakery of authentication bypass. Rapid7 caught active exploitation two weeks after the May patch—because who patches promptly anyway?

articles.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-0257) Under Active Exploitation
articles.summary: Microsoft threatens legal action against researcher Nightmare Eclipse for responsible disclosure, because nothing says 'we value security' like weaponizing lawyers against white hats. Corporate intimidation meets vulnerability research in the worst possible way.
